ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that God’s signs came clearly but the person ignored and failed to consider them, so he is left in blindness and punishment in return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r7.anchor: كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r8.claim: Forgetting here means abandoning the signs, and being forgotten means being left in punishment rather than suffering absent-mindedness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r8.anchor: والنسيان هنا بمعنى الترك لا بمعنى الذهول، ومعنى تنسى تترك في العذاب

DURR-FULL:v5p610/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r1.claim: The statement about being forgotten that day refers to the Fire.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r1.claim: The unbeliever had been given God's signs but forgot them by abandoning belief; accordingly, God leaves him in Hell.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r1.anchor: فتركتها ولم تؤمن بها { وكذلك اليوم تنسى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.claim: The apparent contrast with Qāf 50:22 is resolved because people fail to recognize their blindness in earthly life but will recognize it when reality is unveiled at Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p81/r5.anchor: The answer is that there is no discrepancy.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r1.claim: Although the word glossed here means to ignore, Islahi says the ignored revelations leave the people's eyes shut and their complaint useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r1.anchor: They remain shut. Their complaint is of no use.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r2.claim: Because they ignored God's revelations, they deserve to be ignored in return; their complaint cannot undo that fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r2.anchor: Their complaint is of no use.

SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows كذلك to mean a gathering like that, with an omitted noun indicating the manner of gathering.
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r1.anchor: في موضع نصب أي: حشرا مثل ذلك، أو فعلنا مثل ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r2.claim: Another estimate is an omitted verb: we acted in that same way.
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r2.anchor: أو فعلنا مثل ذلك، أو إتيانا مثل ذلك، أو جزاء مثل إعراضك أو نسيانا ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa also gives arrival like that, or retribution matching the addressee's turning away or forgetting, as possible explanations.
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r3.anchor: أو إتيانا مثل ذلك، أو جزاء مثل إعراضك أو نسيانا ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r4.claim: These estimates make the kāf accusative either as a verbal noun or as a direct object.
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r4.anchor: وهذه الأوجه التي قالها تكون الكاف في بعضها نصبا على المصدر، وفي بعضها نصبا

SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives only the direct-object parse, meaning you acted in that manner.
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r5.anchor: ولم يذكر الزمخشري فيه غير المفعول به فقال: " أي: مثل ذلك فعلت أنت،

SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that God's clear, illuminating signs came, but the addressee did not view them reflectively.
SAMIN-DURR:20:126/r6.anchor: ثم فسر بأن آياتنا أتتك واضحة مستنيرة فلم تنظر إليها بعين المعتبر ".

ZAJJAJ:v3p379/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p379/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p379/r1.claim: You are left in the Fire just as you left God's signs behind.
ZAJJAJ:v3p379/r1.anchor: أي كذلك تترك في النار كما تركت آياتنا.

ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.claim: On Resurrection Day the sinner asks why he is blind despite having had sight; God answers that he ignored the divine messages and is now forgotten.
ASAD-NOTES:20:125/r1.anchor: O my Sustainer! Why hast Thou raised me up blind, whereas [on earth]

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses ḍank only here as a warning to those who turn from God’s reminder, who will be raised blind.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p498/r2.anchor: والقرآن لم يستعمل ضنكاً إلا في هذا الموضع، نذيراً لمن أعرض عن ذكره تعالى، يحشره سبحانه يوم القيامة أعمى.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r1.claim: Mujahid explains that the person forgot God’s signs by leaving them behind.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها ﴾ قال فتركتها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says that being forgotten on that Day means being left in the Fire.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها ﴾ قال فتركتها ﴿ وكذلك اليوم تنسى ﴾ وكذلك اليوم تترك في النار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi treats the kāf as extra, as in mithluka lā yabkhal; dhālika points to the manner of arrival, so the clear signs came to the person in that striking way.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r1.anchor: الكاف مقحمة كما في مثلك لا يبخل وذلك إشارة إلى مصدر أتتك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari does not treat the kāf as extra: dhālika points to the person’s being resurrected blind, just as he acted, so he is treated accordingly.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r2.anchor: وعند الزمخشري لا إقحام وذلك إشارة إلى حشرة أعمى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r3.claim: God’s statement answers the implied question “What did I do?”: the signs came to the person, but he forgot them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r3.anchor: جواب سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل : يا رب ما فعلت أنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r4.claim: Forgetting means abandoning the signs as if wholly forgotten, or becoming blind to them; the effect (forgetting) is named for its cause (turning away).
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r4.anchor: أي تركتها ترك المنسي الذي لايذكر اصلا والمراد فعميت عنها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r5.claim: The second dhālika points to the neglect implied by nasiya, and the kāf keeps its ordinary sense: as the person neglected the signs in life, he is left in blindness today as fitting recompense.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#2/r5.anchor: النسيان المفهوم من نسيتها والكاف على ظاهرها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r1.claim: Some take the kāf as meaning “because of,” like the proposed reading of “remember Him as He guided you” in 2:198.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r1.anchor: وقيل : الكاف بمعنى اللام إلا جلية كما قيل في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r2.claim: The abandonment continues until God removes the blindness and the person sees Judgment Day’s terrors and the Fire, becoming punishment upon punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r2.anchor: ثم يزال العمى عنه فيرى أهوال القيامة ويشاهد النار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r3.claim: Al-Alusi links later sight of the Fire to the verse saying criminals see it and realize they will fall into it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r3.anchor: كما قال سبحانه ( ورأى المجرمون النار فظنوا أنهم مواقعوها )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r11.claim: The verse does not prove that merely forgetting the Qur’an or one verse is a major sin: if signs include Qur’anic verses, “forgetting” here means abandoning them and not believing them.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r11.anchor: وليس في الآية دليل كما يتوهم على عد نسيان القرآن أو آية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r12.speaker: الرافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r12.claim: Al-Rafiʿi counts forgetting the Qur’an or a verse as a major sin; al-Alusi says al-Nawawi’s wording in al-Rawda seems to favor that view.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r12.anchor: كما ذهب إليه الإمام الرافعي ويشعر كلام الإمام النوري في الروضة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r13.speaker: أبو شامة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r13.claim: Abu Shama interprets traditions condemning forgetfulness of Qur’anic material as condemning failure to act on it; those counting literal forgetting major condition it on laziness and disregard, as al-Balqini and al-Zarkashi explain.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p278#3/r13.anchor: نعم تجوز أبو شامة شيخ النووي فحمل النسيان في الأحاديث الواردة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r2.claim: The signs were forgotten in the sense that the person abandoned and turned away from them; on this day he is left in the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r2.anchor: أي كما {أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها} فتركتها وأعرضت عنها، {وكذلك اليوم تنسى} تترك في النار.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says they have forgotten what is good, while not forgetting the punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: نسوا من الخير ولم ينسوا من العذاب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r1.claim: The opening means that God treated the person in just that way; the verse then explains what that means.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r1.anchor: أي مثل ذلك فعلت ثم فسره فقال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r2.claim: Forgetting God's clear signs means becoming blind to them and leaving them unattended.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r2.anchor: فعميت عنها وتركتها غير منظور إليها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r3.claim: Just as the person neglected the signs, he is now left in blindness and punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:126/r3.anchor: ومثل تركك إياها. { اليوم تنسى } تترك في العمى والعذاب.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.claim: Kadhālika may mean that the person acted shamefully in this way in life, or that matters were as he said; the reply then explains the first reading and gives the cause on the second.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r3.anchor: مثل هذا الفعل الشنيع فعلت في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r4.claim: Forgetting God's signs means treating them with the neglect of something unseen, making oneself blind in sight and insight, as those whose eyes were veiled from remembrance.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r4.anchor: معاملة المنسي الذي لا يبصره صاحبه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r5.claim: Today the person is left in blindness and the Fire's misery, like an object no one sees or attends to.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r5.anchor: تترك على ما أنت عليه بالعمى والشقاء بالنار

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r5.claim: Mujahid explains that today the person is left in the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r5.anchor: {قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى} قال: تترك في النار

DURR-FULL:v5p609/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r9.claim: Al-Suddi says the person forgot God's signs by abandoning the duty to act on them.
DURR-FULL:v5p609/r9.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها} يقول: تركتها أن تعمل بها

BURSEVI:v5p339/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339/r7.claim: The revealed verses, proofs of divine power, and signs of oneness were clear and apparent to everyone.
BURSEVI:v5p339/r7.anchor: آيات الكتاب أو دلائل القدرة وعلامات الوحدة واضحة نيرة بحيث لا تخفى على أحد

BURSEVI:v5p339/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339/r8.claim: Forgetting means becoming blind to the signs and abandoning them like something utterly forgotten.
BURSEVI:v5p339/r8.anchor: أي : عميت عنها وتركتها ترك المنسي الذي لا يذكر أصلا

BURSEVI:v5p339/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339/r9.claim: As he neglected the signs in life, he is left blind in punishment as fitting recompense; the blindness, muteness, and deafness are eventually removed so he sees the terrors and his place in Hell.
BURSEVI:v5p339/r9.anchor: تترك في العمى والعذاب جزاء وفاقا لكن لا أبدا كما قيل بل إلى ما شاء الله ثم يزيله عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.claim: Resurrection blindness depicts worldly blindness to guidance and salvation; it marks God's anger and exclusion from mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r4.anchor: تمثيلا لحالته الحسية يومئذ بحالته المعنوية في الدنيا ، وهي حالة عدم النظر في وسائل الهدى والنجاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.claim: Blindness in the first instance is figurative, while blindness at resurrection is real.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r5.anchor: فأعمى الأول مجاز وأعمى الثاني حقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.claim: The question begins a new sentence, and God's reply is separated because it continues the dialogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r6.anchor: قال رب لم حشرتني أعمى } مستأنفة استئنافا ابتدائيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r7.claim: The verse indicates that humanity was warned from its beginning against misguidance and polytheism, with warning embedded in human nature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r7.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على أن الله أبلغ الإنسان من يوم نشأته التحذير من الضلال والشرك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r8.speaker: كثير من علماء الإسلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r8.claim: Many Muslim scholars hold that polytheists among peoples living between revealed laws deserve punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r8.anchor: قال كثير من علماء الإسلام : بأن الإشراك بالله من الأمم التي يكون في الفتر بين الشرائع مستحق صاحبه العقاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r9.speaker: أهل السنة والمعتزلة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r9.claim: Ahl al-Sunna and all Muʿtazilites hold that reason makes knowledge of God obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r9.anchor: وقال جماعة من أهل السنة والمعتزلة قاطبة : إن معرفة الله واجبة بالعقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r10.claim: The Qur'an invokes this warning to alert its hearers not to turn away from God's remembrance and to warn them of a like fate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r10.anchor: المقصود من ذكرها في القرآن تنبيه المخاطبين بالقرآن إلى الحذر من الإعراض عن ذكر الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r11.claim: 'Likewise' points back to the questioned blindness: the condemned had forgotten God's signs and refused to consider them when urged, so their fate fits their conduct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p331/r11.anchor: مثل ذلك الحال التي تساءلت عن سببها كنت نسيت آياتنا حين أتتك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.claim: The passage uses three instances of ellipsis: the gathering also leaves the person forgotten, and the reply implies prior blindness to the signs as well as present blindness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.anchor: وقد ظهر من نظم الآية أن فيها ثلاثة احتباكات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r2.claim: Forgetting in both places is a metaphor or metonymy for being deprived of mercy's benefits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r2.anchor: والنسيان في الموضعين مستعمل كناية أو استعارة في الحرمان من حظوظ الرحمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r16.claim: “Thus” points to the blindness that came upon him: God's signs came in worldly life, but he neglected them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68#2/r16.anchor: ذلك إشارة إلى العمى الذي حل به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r1.claim: Here forgetting means neglect, not mental lapse; تُنسى means to be left in punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r1.anchor: والنسيان في هذه الآية بمعنى الترك ولا مدخل للذهول في هذا الموضع، وتنسى بمعنى تترك في العذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r2.claim: A report says the verse was revealed concerning al-Murshi.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69/r2.anchor: وروي أن هذه الآية نزلت في المرشي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#2/r1.claim: The person left God's signs and did not believe in them; as he abandoned them in worldly life, he is abandoned in the Fire today.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#2/r1.anchor: أي فتركتها ولم تؤمن بها وكما تركتها في الدنيا تترك اليوم في النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r5.claim: God's signs had come to him, but he treated them as if he did not remember them, deliberately neglecting and ignoring them after they were conveyed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r5.anchor: لما أعرضت عن آيات الله، وعاملتها معاملة من لم يذكرها، بعد بلاغها إليك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r6.claim: God treats him as forgotten in return, as in the verse that says He forgets them as they forgot their meeting with this Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r6.anchor: فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r8.claim: Forgetting Quranic wording while understanding its meaning and observing it is outside this particular threat, though another threat applies and the Sunnah warns severely against it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r8.anchor: فأما نسيان لفظ القرآن مع فهم معناه والقيام بمقتضاه، فليس داخلا في هذا الوعيد الخاص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r9.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r9.claim: Ahmad transmits from Sa'd ibn Ubada that a man who reads the Quran and then forgets it will meet God with the condition described as ajdham.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r9.anchor: عن رجل، عن سعد بن عبادة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r10.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r10.claim: Ahmad also gives the same Prophetic warning through Ubadah ibn al-Samit instead of Sa'd ibn Ubada.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324/r10.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فذكر مثله سواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r1.claim: The Prophet says a ruler over ten will be brought shackled on Judgment Day, freed only by justice, and a man who learns then forgets the Quran will meet God maimed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r1.anchor: عن عيسى بن فائد، عن عبادة بن الصامت قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما من أمير عشرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r2.claim: Abu Awana also transmits the Ubadah report from Yazid with disagreement in its chain; Ibn Kathir accepts it for exhortative warning, especially if another route corroborates it, as Abu Ubayd says.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r2.anchor: وكذا رواه أبو عوانة، عن يزيد بن أبي زياد، ففيه اختلاف، لكن هذا في باب الترهيب مقبول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r3.claim: Anas’s report says the Prophet was shown his community’s rewards, even removing dirt from a mosque, and saw no sin greater than forgetting a Quranic verse or surah entrusted to someone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: حدثت عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " عرضت علي أجور أمتي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r4.claim: A report attributed to Salman calls forgetting an entrusted Quranic surah the greatest sin the community will bring on Judgment Day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r4.anchor: وحدثت عن سلمان الفارسي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن أكبر ذنب توافي به أمتي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r5.claim: Anas’s fuller report is transmitted by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Abu Ya‘la, al-Bazzar and others; al-Tirmidhi calls it gharīb, al-Bukhari found it strange, and al-Darimi questioned al-Mutallib’s hearing from Anas. Ibn Kathir notes an alternate route through al-Zuhri.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r5.anchor: وقد روى أبو داود والترمذي وأبو يعلى والبزار وغيرهم من حديث ابن أبي رواد، عن ابن جريج، عن المطلب بن عبد الله بن حنطب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.claim: Some commentators include neglecting Quran recitation, allowing it to be forgotten, and failing to care for it within turning away from God’s remembrance; Ibn Kathir says this is part, though not the whole, of the verse’s intent and is grave negligence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r6.anchor: وقد أدخل بعض المفسرين هذا المعنى في قوله تعالى: {ومن أعرض عن ذكري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r7.claim: The Prophet commanded people to keep reviewing the Quran, which slips from men’s breasts faster than camels escape.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p72/r7.anchor: ولهذا قال عليه السلام: "تعاهدوا القرآن"، وفي لفظ: " استذكروا القرآن، فإنه أشد تفصيا من صدور الرجال من النعم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r11.claim: God’s clear signs went unheeded; the person failed to reflect, abandoned them, and was blind to them, so God leaves him blind that day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p95/r11.anchor: آياتنا أتتك واضحة مستنيرة ، فلم تنظر إليها بعين المعتبر

MUQATIL:20:126-127/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r1.claim: The signs that came to him were the Qur'an's signs.

MUQATIL:20:126-127/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r2.claim: Forgetting here means abandoning belief in the Qur'anic signs.
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r2.anchor: { فنسيتها } يعنى فتركت إيمانا بآيات القرآن

MUQATIL:20:126-127/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r3.claim: In the afterlife he is left in the Fire, never taken out and no longer remembered by God.
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r3.anchor: { وكذلك اليوم تنسى } [آية: 126] فى الآخرة تترك فى النار، ولا تخرج منها، ولا نذكرك.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r1.claim: “Thus” means that the person acted in the same way.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r2.claim: God’s clear signs came, but the person failed to consider them and turned away as though blind to them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r2.anchor: أتتك آياتنا واضحة فلم تنظر إليها بعين المعتبر وتركتها وعميت عنها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r3.claim: Likewise, on this Day God leaves the person to his deeds and does not lift the covering from his eyes.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#3/r3.anchor: فكذلك اليو نتركك على عمالك ولا يزيل غطاءه عن عينيك

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r5.claim: God's signs are proofs of His oneness and power.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r6.claim: Forgetting here means abandoning the signs, failing to consider them, and turning away from them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r6.anchor: أي تركتها ولم تنظر فيها، وأعرضت عنها.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r7.claim: Being forgotten today means being left in punishment, namely Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r7.anchor: أي تترك في العذاب يريد جهنم

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.claim: One explanation is that God makes the rejecter blind as requital for abandoning and turning away from guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r8.anchor: أنه تعالى إنما أنزل به هذا العمى جزاء على تركه اتباع الهدى والإعراض عنه

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.claim: Alternatively, souls that leave their bodies ignorant and disconnected from spiritual beings retain that state, and their spiritual pain intensifies; their worldly rejection of evidence explains the blindness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r9.anchor: هو أن الأرواح البشرية إذا فارقت أبدانها جاهلة ضالة عن الاتصال بالروحانيات بقيت على تلك الحالة

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.claim: Those who interpret constricted life as worldly take the passage to pair worldly hardship for turning from remembrance with blindness in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r10.anchor: ومن فسر المعيشة الضنك بالضيق في الدنيا ، قال إنه تعالى

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.claim: Citing a report that a person meets God in the state in which they lived, Qushayri says the worldly blind of heart and the ignorant are resurrected in that condition.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r1.anchor: في الخبر : ( من كان بحالة لقي الله بها ) فمن كان في الدنيا أعمى القلب يحشر على حالته

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.claim: Those who neglect reflection on God's signs in this life are left in punishment without mercy in the next; God's practice repays each person according to their deeds.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r3.anchor: وكما يتركون - اليوم - التدبر في آياته يتركون غدا في العقوبة من غير رحمة على ضعف حالاتهم

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.claim: Qushayri urges people to reflect, take heed, and stop their bad conduct instead of running through heedlessness without turning back.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r4.anchor: أفلا ينظرون فيتفكرون ؟ ثم إذا استبصروا أفلا يعتبرون ؟ وإذا اعتبروا أفلا يزدجرون

QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.claim: Although happiness and misery are decreed and God's knowledge encompasses what will occur, striving and effort also belong to the decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p281/r6.anchor: فالسعي والجهد ، والانكماش والجد . . متى تنفع ؟ لكنه من القسمة أيضا ما ظهر

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r7.claim: Forgetting God's signs means abandoning and disbelieving in them, namely the proofs brought by His messengers.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r7.anchor: To forget Our signs (v. 126) means to abandon and disbelieve in God’s signs

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r8.claim: The commentary refers to other passages on God forgetting the disbelievers on the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r8.anchor: For God’s “forgetting”the disbelievers on the Last Day, see 7:51c and 45:34c

TAB-FULL:v16p203/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r1.claim: God's signs are His proofs, evidences, and clarification in His Book; the sinner forgot them by abandoning and rejecting them and failing to act on them.
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r1.anchor: فكما نسيت آياتنا في الدنيا، فتركتها وأعرضت عنها، فكذلك اليوم ننساك، فنتركك في النار

TAB-FULL:v16p203/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r2.claim: The phrase kathālika atatka means thus they came to you.

TAB-FULL:v16p203/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r3.claim: Just as the person abandoned God's signs in worldly life, God leaves him today in the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r3.anchor: فكما نسيت آياتنا في الدنيا، فتركتها وأعرضت عنها، فكذلك اليوم ننساك، فنتركك في النار

TAB-FULL:v16p203/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r4.claim: Abu Salih explains being forgotten today as being in the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح، في قوله: {وكذلك اليوم تنسى} [طه: 126] قال: في النار

TAB-FULL:v16p203/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r5.claim: Mujahid glosses forgetting God's signs as abandoning them and being forgotten today as being left in the Fire.
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها} [طه: 126] قال: فتركتها

TAB-FULL:v16p203/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r6.claim: Qatada says the person is forgotten with respect to good, but not with respect to evil.
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، {قال كذلك أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها وكذلك اليوم تنسى} [طه: 126] قال: نسي من الخير، ولم ينس من الشر

TAB-FULL:v16p203/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r7.claim: Al-Tabari says Qatada's gloss is close to Abu Salih's and Mujahid's: being left in the Fire is the greatest evil for them.
TAB-FULL:v16p203/r7.anchor: وهذا القول الذي قاله قتادة قريب المعنى مما قاله أبو صالح ومجاهد، لأن تركه إياهم في النار أعظم الشر لهم

TABATABAI:20:126#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r1.claim: “Thus” answers the question about blindness: as the signs came and the person forgot them, God leaves him today without sight or guidance; the response repays his act in kind.
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r1.anchor: إنما جازيناك في هذا اليوم بمثل ما فعلت في الدنيا كما قال تعالى وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها

TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.claim: The close echoes Adam's forgetfulness: his garden story prefigures his descendants, the tree prohibition represents later divine guidance, and their sins are forgetting God's reminders; unlike them, Adam faced an advisory ban before religious law.
TABATABAI:20:126#2/r2.anchor: وانعطف بذلك آخر الكلام إلى أوله وهو معصية آدم التي سماها نسيانا لعهده

TABRISI:20:126-129/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:126-129/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:126-129/r7.claim: God answers that Muhammad, the Qur’an, and the proofs came to the person, who turned away and left them behind; threatened forgetting here means neglect, since involuntary forgetfulness is not an act.
TABRISI:20:126-129/r7.anchor: جاءك محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن والدلائل فأعرضت عنها وتعرضت لنسيانها

TABRISI:20:126-129/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:126-129/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:126-129/r8.claim: The threat is for neglect rather than involuntary forgetting, which is not an act people can be punished for.
TABRISI:20:126-129/r8.anchor: فإن النسيان ليس من فعل الإنسان فيتوعد عليه

TABRISI:20:126-129/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:126-129/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:126-129/r9.claim: The person is left as though forgotten, enduring punishment that does not end.
TABRISI:20:126-129/r9.anchor: أي تصير بمنزلة من ترك كالمنسي بعذاب لا يفنى

TABRISI:20:126-129/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:126-129/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:126-129/r10.claim: Another view says the person was blind in heart, ignored God’s signs, and is now left in torment as he had left God’s commands as though forgotten.
TABRISI:20:126-129/r10.anchor: وقيل: معناه كما حشرتك أعمى لتكون فضيحة كنت أعمى القلب فتركت آياتي

THALABI:v6p265/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r17.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p265/r17.claim: The reply says the person abandoned and turned away from the signs when they came, so is now left in the Fire.
THALABI:v6p265/r17.anchor: كما أتتك آياتنا فنسيتها فتركتها وأعرضت عنها وكذلك اليوم تنسى تترك في النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r1.claim: God answers the disbeliever: this is how things are, as you now see.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r1.anchor: قال الله مجيبا لهذا الكافر كذلك الأمر كما ترى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي، أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Kalbī, and the exegetes say the person abandoned God's signs and did not believe; correspondingly, he is left in the Fire today.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.anchor: هذا قول ابن عباس، والكلبي، وأهل التفسير

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r6.claim: God explains that His signs had come to the person in worldly life.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p289/r6.anchor: أي: لأنه أتتك آياتنا في الدنيا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r1.claim: The person left God’s signs and did not believe in them.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r2.claim: Being forgotten on that day means being left in the Fire.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r3.speaker: عكرمة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r3.claim: Ikrimah also says the phrase means being in the Fire.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r3.anchor: عن جابر، عن عكرمة قال: {وكذلك اليوم تنسى} [طه: 126] قال: في النار.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r4.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r4.claim: Qatadah says the person is left without good, not spared from evil.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: نسي من الخير أي: ترك من الخير ولم ينس من الشر،

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r1.claim: Readerly misapprehension has degrees: sometimes resemblance becomes belief, while weaker resemblance produces only a passing impression.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r1.anchor: أن التوهم على ضر بين ضرب يستحكم حتى يبلغ ان يصير اعتقادا وضرب لا يبلغ ذلك المبلغ ولكنه شىء يجري في الخاطر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r2.claim: Padding is condemned because it contributes nothing, but a supposedly expendable phrase that unexpectedly benefits the listener is no longer empty padding.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r2.anchor: وأما الحشو فإنما كره وذم وأنكر ورد لأنه خلا من الفائدة ولم يحل منه بعائدة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r3.claim: Metaphor is a kind of simile and representation: comparison is an analogy grasped by the intellect and heart, not by hearing alone.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r3.anchor: أما الاستعارة فهي ضرب من التشبيه ونمط من التمثيل والتشبيه قياس

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r4.claim: Antithesis is semantic opposition between ideas; it cannot arise merely from opposing word forms.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r4.anchor: وأما التطبيق فأمره أبين وكونه معنويا أجلى وأظهر فهو مقابلة الشىء بضده

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r5.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line is difficult because its word order fails to follow the order of thought, forcing the hearer to rearrange it and disrupting the image like badly assembled geometric parts.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p14/r5.anchor: لم يرتب الألفاظ في الذكر على موجب ترتيب المعاني في الفكر فكد وكدر ومنع السامع أن يفهم الغرض
